name: Atlanta Botanical Garden
unique: Thirty acres of display gardens beside Piedmont Park, with a canopy walk, a tropical conservatory and a carnivorous plant house, plus blockbuster sculpture shows in summer.
buzz: The canopy walk is the kid winner and the orchid house is the quiet one. Book the lights show in December weeks ahead.

name: High Museum of Art
unique: A Richard Meier building with a Renzo Piano wing, holding a strong folk art collection, European painting and a photography program that punches above the city's size.
buzz: The folk art and the architecture are the reasons. Free admission on some evenings, so check before you buy.

name: National Center for Civil and Human Rights
unique: An interactive museum where you sit at a lunch counter and hear the threats, then follow the movement from Atlanta to the global fight for human rights.
buzz: The lunch counter simulation is the experience people describe for years. Give it two hours and go early.

name: Chick-fil-A College Football Hall of Fame
unique: A museum with a field where you run drills, throw passes and kick field goals, plus a wall of every college helmet and the stories of the inductees.
buzz: The interactive field is the point and adults have as much fun as kids. Allow two hours.

name: World of Coca-Cola
unique: A brand museum with the vault, a bottling line and a tasting room of international sodas, next to the aquarium and the civil rights center.
buzz: It is corporate and cheerful, and the tasting room is the fun part. Skip if you hate crowds, go early if you do not.

name: Sweet Auburn Curb Market
unique: A 1924 municipal market where Black farmers once sold from the curb, now a hall of soul food counters, butcher stalls and a bakery under one roof.
buzz: The oxtail and the fried fish are the local picks. It is a working market, not a food hall, and that is the charm.

name: The Varsity
unique: The world's largest drive in, open since 1928, where the counter staff shout What'll ya have and the chili dogs and frosted oranges have not changed.
buzz: It is an institution, not a quiet meal. Order the chili dog and a frosted orange, and do not ask for a menu at the counter.

name: Chattahoochee Nature Center
unique: A nature center on the river with rehab birds of prey, a beaver pond, boardwalks and canoe programs, twenty minutes from midtown.
buzz: The hawks and owls are the hit and the trails are easy. Check the river programs in summer.

name: Atlanta History Center
unique: A campus with the 1928 Swan House, a Civil War exhibit, a reconstructed farm and gardens, telling Atlanta's story from the Creek land to the civil rights era.
buzz: The Swan House and the farm are the two poles and both are good. The Cyclorama is the older attraction, now restored.

name: Michael C. Carlos Museum
unique: An Emory museum with Egyptian mummies, Greek pottery and South American gold, in a Michael Graves building with a quiet courtyard.
buzz: The mummy gallery is the draw and the collection is deeper than expected for a university museum. Free on some days.

name: Eddie's Attic
unique: A listening room above a Decatur storefront where John Mayer and the Indigo Girls played early shows, with tables, a bar and no talking during sets.
buzz: The sound is excellent and the room is small enough to see hands on strings. Buy tickets ahead for name acts.

name: David J. Sencer CDC Museum
unique: A museum inside the CDC campus tracing disease outbreaks, the smallpox campaign and the epidemiologists who chase them, with a real iron lung and a global map room.
buzz: Surprisingly gripping for a government museum, and free. Bring photo ID for security, and check the open days.

name: Decatur Square
unique: A courthouse square with a bandstand, a farmers market, bookshops and a restaurant row, in a town that feels like a small college city inside the metro.
buzz: The square is walkable and busy on weekends, with a farmers market on Saturdays. Parking is easier in the deck.

name: Truist Park and The Battery
unique: A ballpark with a surrounding block of restaurants, bars and a plaza that stays busy even when the team is away, plus a battery of pre game music.
buzz: Buy the cheap seats and walk the concourse. The Battery is the pre game and post game plan, and the food is better than ballpark default.

name: Gone With the Wind Museum
customer: Film fans, history people, curiosity seekers
unique: A collection of costumes, posters and foreign editions of the novel, including Margaret Mitchell's own annotated copy, in a restored train depot.
buzz: For fans of the book and the movie, and for anyone interested in how the myth was sold. It is small and unapologetically specific.

name: Earl Smith Strand Theatre
unique: A restored 1935 movie palace on Marietta Square with a neon marquee, showing films, concerts and community theater under a starry ceiling.
buzz: The room is the attraction and the balcony seats are the pick. Check for classic film nights.

name: Gwinnett Environmental and Heritage Center
unique: A LEED certified center with a 3D theater, a treetop canopy walk and exhibits on water, energy and the Piedmont forest, on a reclaimed site.
buzz: The canopy walk and the water table are the kid hits. It is a good rainy day option with real content.

name: Hudgens Center for Art and Learning
unique: A community art center with galleries, studios and classes, showing regional artists and teaching pottery and painting to anyone who signs up.
buzz: Free or cheap, with changing shows and a real studio program. Check the class schedule if you want to make something.

name: McDaniel Farm Park
unique: A preserved 1930s subsistence farm with a farmhouse, barn, chicken yard and garden, sitting in the middle of suburban Gwinnett.
buzz: A quiet hour with goats and old tools, free and flat. Good for small kids and a picnic.

name: Spivey Hall
unique: A 400 seat concert hall on a commuter campus with acoustics that touring chamber musicians compare to the best rooms in Europe.
buzz: People drive from across the metro for the sound, and student tickets are cheap. Look for the jazz and world music series.

name: Road to Tara Museum
unique: A Gone With the Wind collection in the old Jonesboro depot, with costumes, memorabilia and the local history the novel borrowed.
buzz: Small and earnest, best paired with Stately Oaks next door. Fans get the most from it.

name: Stately Oaks Plantation
unique: A Greek Revival house museum with outbuildings, a one room school and a kitchen garden, used as a model for Twelve Oaks in the film.
buzz: The guided tour covers the plantation economy and the enslaved workers, not just the furniture. Check hours before driving out.

name: Atlanta Motor Speedway
unique: A 1.54 mile quad oval south of the city with NASCAR weekends, a dirt track next door and a Wednesday night short track series.
buzz: The spring race is the big one and the infield is a scene. The short track nights are cheaper and closer to the action.

name: Nash Farm Battlefield
unique: A preserved battlefield and farm where the last major cavalry battle of the Atlanta campaign was fought, with earthworks, a museum and a walking trail.
buzz: Quiet and free, with a small museum that explains the cavalry fight. Good for a history hour off the interstate.

name: Heritage Park
unique: A county park with a lake, a walking trail, a playground and a disc golf course, plus a small veterans memorial.
buzz: A plain, well kept park for a picnic and a loop. Not a destination, but a good leg stretch.

name: The Villages Amphitheater
unique: An outdoor amphitheater on the square with a summer concert series, lawn seating and a small town crowd.
buzz: Bring a blanket and a cooler. The shows are affordable and the sound is good for an outdoor room.

name: The Ridge Nature Area
unique: A wooded nature area with ridge trails, a creek and a boardwalk, one of the few real hikes inside the southern metro.
buzz: Quiet and rolling, with good spring wildflowers. The trails are not paved, so wear shoes.

name: Senoia Walking Dead Tour
unique: A guided walk through the small town that played Alexandria in The Walking Dead, with the storefronts, the wall and the filming stories.
buzz: Fans love it and non fans still get a good small town walk. Book ahead and wear comfortable shoes.

name: Chattahoochee Bend State Park
unique: One of Georgia's newest and largest state parks, with a bend of the Chattahoochee, riverside campsites, a canoe launch and bluff trails.
buzz: Quiet and spacious, with real river access. The walk to the bend is the hike to do.

name: Newnan Courthouse Square
unique: A square of antebellum and Victorian buildings with a gold dome courthouse, independent shops and a restaurant row, in a town that calls itself the City of Homes.
buzz: The architecture is the draw and the square is walkable. Look for the old theater and the court square fountain.

name: Sweetwater Creek State Park
unique: A park with the ruins of the New Manchester textile mill on the creek, burned by Sherman's troops, reached by a trail through pine and floodplain.
buzz: The mill ruins are the photo and the story, and the red trail is a real hike with a rocky descent. Go early for parking.

name: Boundary Waters Park
unique: A county park with a lake, a beach, a ropes course, disc golf and a water park, on the site of a former reservoir.
buzz: The beach and splash pad are the summer draw. It is a locals' park with plenty of parking.

name: Pickett's Mill Battlefield
unique: One of the best preserved Civil War battlefields in the country, with original earthworks, a ravine and trails where the fighting happened in dense woods.
buzz: The terrain explains the battle better than any map. Quiet, shaded and rarely crowded.

name: Silver Comet Trail
unique: A paved rail trail running from Smyrna to the Alabama line, over trestles and through tunnels, built on the old Seaboard Air Line grade.
buzz: Flat and fast, good for long rides and beginner skaters. Start at the Dallas or Hiram trailhead for parking.

name: Dallas Courthouse Square
unique: A small courthouse square with a Confederate monument, old storefronts and a theater, in the county seat of a fast growing metro county.
buzz: A ten minute walk, best paired with Pickett's Mill. The old jail is the curiosity.

name: Gibbs Gardens
unique: Three hundred acres of designed gardens with a Japanese garden, a daffodil hill, a manor house and a seven acre water garden, built by a retired landscaper.
buzz: The scale is astonishing and the spring daffodils are the peak. Wear walking shoes and allow three hours.

name: Blankets Creek Mountain Bike Trails
unique: A stacked loop trail system on Corps of Engineers land with flowy berms, rock gardens and a beginner loop, maintained by local riders.
buzz: The trails are well built and signed, with a skills loop for beginners. Check the trail status after rain.

name: Canton Courthouse Square
unique: A hilltop square with a marble courthouse, a gazebo and a row of shops, in the town that calls itself the gateway to the mountains.
buzz: The square is small and well kept, with a farmers market in season. Good stop before Gibbs Gardens.

name: Sawnee Mountain Preserve
unique: A preserve with a boardwalk, a visitor center and a summit trail to a rock outcrop with a view over Lake Lanier and the Blue Ridge foothills.
buzz: The summit trail is short and steep with a big payoff. The Indian Seats rock is the photo.

name: Lake Lanier Islands
unique: An island resort on Lake Lanier with a water park, a beach, a golf course, zip lines and rental boats, an hour from Atlanta.
buzz: The water park is the summer draw and the beach is calm. Book parking and rentals ahead on holiday weekends.

name: Panola Mountain State Park
unique: A granite monadnock preserved as a national natural landmark, with ranger led hikes to the summit and a boardwalk around the base.
buzz: The summit is only open on ranger tours, which is why it stays pristine. Book the tour and bring water.

name: Oxford College
unique: The original Emory campus, with brick halls, a quad and a cemetery, in a tiny town that still feels like the 19th century.
buzz: A quiet, pretty walk under old oaks. The cemetery holds early Methodist leaders and Civil War dead.

name: Covington Square
unique: A courthouse square that has played Mystic Falls in The Vampire Diaries and a dozen other shows, with the clock tower, the alley and the storefronts fans recognize.
buzz: The film map is free at the visitor center and the square is walkable. Weekends bring tour groups.

name: Etowah Indian Mounds
unique: Six earthen mounds built by the Mississippian culture a thousand years ago, with a plaza, a village site and a museum of copper and shell art.
buzz: The scale of the mounds is the surprise, and the museum explains the chiefdom well. Climb the largest mound for the view.

name: Tellus Science Museum
unique: A science museum with a real T. rex, a mineral gallery, a planetarium and a fossil dig, plus a collection of vintage cars and aircraft.
buzz: The dinosaur and the gem room are the hits, and the planetarium shows are included. Allow three hours.

name: Booth Western Art Museum
unique: A museum of Western art with cowboy and Native American painting, a presidential gallery and a sculpture court, in a converted mill.
buzz: Far more interesting than the subject sounds, and the presidential letters gallery is a surprise.

name: Red Top Mountain State Park
unique: A peninsula of trails and campsites on Lake Allatoona, with a beach, a marina and a ridge trail through pine and hardwood.
buzz: The lake views and the easy trails make it a good family day. Summer weekends fill the beach early.

name: Don Carter State Park
unique: The newest state park on Lake Lanier, with a sandy beach, rental cabins, paddle craft and trails through hardwood above the lake.
buzz: Clean, spacious and less developed than the islands. The beach is the summer draw.

name: Elachee Nature Science Center
unique: A nature center with live animals, a discovery room and trails into the Chicopee Woods, one of the largest protected forests in the metro.
buzz: Good for kids and cheap, with real trails behind the building. Check the weekend programs.

name: Lake Lanier Olympic Park
unique: The 1996 Olympic rowing venue, still a working boathouse and regatta course, with a beach, a tower and paddle rentals on the lake.
buzz: You can rent a kayak and paddle the Olympic course. The tower view is free and the regattas are fun to watch.

name: Adamson Square
unique: A courthouse square with a fountain, a theater, coffee shops and a music venue, next to a university campus in west Georgia.
buzz: The square is the town's living room, busy on weekday mornings and cool on summer nights.

name: The AMP at Adamson Square
unique: An outdoor amphitheater on the square with a summer concert series, lawn seats and a lineup of regional rock, country and soul acts.
buzz: Bring a chair and arrive early for a good spot. The sound is solid and the crowd is local.
